content: TaskFlow uses React with TypeScript for its frontend. The build is Vite-based and deployed as static assets behind a CDN.
TaskFlow uses FastAPI with Python 3.11 for its backend. The API service is stateless and scales horizontally behind a load balancer.
PostgreSQL 16 is TaskFlow's canonical source of truth. All durable task state lives in PostgreSQL.
Redis in TaskFlow is only for caching, background job dispatch, and transient state. Redis must never become the canonical database.
The system uses Redis Streams for asynchronous task processing so that task events survive a broker restart.
Redis Pub/Sub is used for task notifications in TaskFlow.
Redis Streams replaced Redis Pub/Sub for durable task event processing. Pub/Sub was dropped because messages published while a consumer was down were lost permanently.
TaskFlow used offset pagination for the task listing API before the task table grew beyond 100,000 records.
The task listing API in TaskFlow currently uses cursor pagination. Cursor pagination is mandatory for task listing.
Cursor pagination was introduced to avoid inconsistent results under concurrent writes. Offset pagination produced inconsistent results and duplicate rows during concurrent task inserts.
Cursor pagination became mandatory for task listing because offset pagination produced inconsistent results during concurrent writes.
Task list queries must use an indexed sort key compatible with cursor pagination, namely created_at together with id.
The authentication system uses short-lived access tokens and rotating refresh tokens. Refresh tokens must be stored in HttpOnly cookies.
A 2026 incident showed that returning refresh tokens in a JSON response body exposes them to JavaScript. Returning refresh tokens in JSON bodies is prohibited.
Access token time to live in TaskFlow is 15 minutes. Refresh token time to live is 30 days.
Passwords are hashed with Argon2id using a per-user salt. Plaintext passwords are never logged.
The API gateway performs request-level rate limiting before requests reach the payment service, limiting each client to 100 requests per minute.
PAYMENT_ERR_4291: the payment service returns HTTP 429 when the Redis rate-limit threshold is exceeded.
PAYMENT_ERR_4292: the payment retry worker returns HTTP 429 after exceeding the retry budget.
PAYMENT_ERR_4921: the payment gateway returns HTTP 492 during upstream validation.
PAYMENT_ERR_1021: the payment service returns HTTP 1021 when authentication token validation fails.
Runbook for PAYMENT_ERR_4291: raise the Redis rate-limit threshold or ask the client to back off. This is a rate limit, not an upstream failure.
TaskFlow background jobs are idempotent. A task may be enqueued more than once without producing duplicate side effects.
Task status changes must create an immutable status-history record. Status history rows are append-only.
WebSocket notifications are used for task assignment and overdue-task updates on the dashboard.
Overdue tasks must appear on the dashboard and trigger a notification to the assigned user.
The TaskFlow project owner prefers TypeScript on the frontend and Python with FastAPI on the backend.
TaskFlow deploys as OCI containers on Kubernetes. The backend runs three replicas behind an internal service.
Database migrations run as a Kubernetes Job before the new backend version rolls out. Migrations must be backward compatible with the previous release.
Rolling back a TaskFlow backend release does not roll back the database. Schema changes must therefore be additive and reversible in a follow-up migration.
The task table has a composite index on (created_at, id) and a partial index on (assignee_id) where status is not done.
An N+1 query in the task list serializer was fixed by eager loading the assignee relationship. List endpoints must not issue one query per row.
The task list endpoint returns an ETag header. Clients revalidate with If-None-Match to avoid refetching unchanged task pages.
February 2026 incident: the task list endpoint returned 500s for ten minutes because a cursor decoding change was deployed without a backwards-compatible default.
March 2026 incident: a cache stampede on the dashboard summary key saturated Redis. A short random jitter was added to cache TTLs.
April 2026 incident: task notifications were lost during a Redis failover because Pub/Sub messages are not durable. This led to the decision to adopt Redis Streams.
The TaskFlow REST API is versioned by URL path prefix, for example /api/v1/tasks. Breaking changes require a new version prefix.
POST /api/v1/tasks accepts an Idempotency-Key header. Replaying the same key within 24 hours returns the original response instead of creating a duplicate task.
TaskFlow API errors use a JSON envelope with code, message, and request_id. Clients match on code, never on message text.
TaskFlow authorizes task reads with row-level security in PostgreSQL scoped to the requesting user's organization.
Task tags are stored as a JSONB array in PostgreSQL with a GIN index. Tags were moved from a join table to JSONB in 2026 to simplify writes.
Task tags were stored in a separate task_tags join table before they were moved to JSONB.
A profiling run showed deep offset pages on the task list took 2.4 seconds at page 500. Cursor pagination brought the same traversal to 40 milliseconds.
A dependency security scan flagged two moderate CVEs in the image processing library. Both were patched in the 4.2 release.
A load test at 2,000 requests per second showed the API gateway rate limiter saturated first, before the payment service.
